label: input token w during copy phase (and at t=0)
explanation: Token detector for input w, gated by phase. Fires on every copy-phase step whose fed-back input is w (about 0.6-1.0 of max), and weakly on w as the very first original token (t=0, about 0.27 of max). It is essentially silent on w at original-phase positions t>=1: a w at t=1 gives only about 0.1, and later original-phase w inputs give nothing. Magnitude is highest when the copy-phase w is the first of a repeated ww pair (about 0.95-1.0); the second w in the pair is lower (about 0.75-0.88). A copied w right after <DEL> reaches about 0.7-0.8. It does not fire on the delimiter or on other tokens, apart from rare weak (about 0.1) activations on copy-phase n. 99% of activation mass is covered and there are no false positives on dev.

issues: Test split checks out: precision 1.0, recall 0.947, F1 0.973, mass recall 0.990. The misses tool found 0 false positives on test.

The two parts were checked on test. Copy-phase w alone: precision 1.0, mass recall 0.927. w at t=0 alone: precision 1.0, mass 0.063, all of it in the lowest activation quartile, which fits the claimed weak ~0.27.

The leftover ~1% of mass is scattered, not systematic. It comes from three sources. (1) w at t=1, with precision 0.13 and about 0.1-0.16 activation; adding t<=1 drops F1 to 0.923. (2) Copy-phase n, with precision 0.033 and about 0.11-0.16. (3) A few hundred weak activations (~0.13) on w at the last original positions (orig_idx 7-8). That third point slightly contradicts the claim that 'later original-phase w inputs give nothing', but the predicate for original-phase w at t>=1 has precision 0.03 and mass 0.005, so it is negligible.

Minor magnitude overclaims. Copy-phase w goes down to about 0.58, not 0.6. In a www run the middle w was the highest (0.91 then 0.99), so 'first of the ww pair is highest' is not universal. Neither changes the label.
